items.content_html:
Overview

This PR improves documentation completeness by adding self-contained examples and migration guides to deprecated HTML elements and Web Audio API interfaces that previously only referred to factory methods or other pages.

Changes Made

Deprecated HTML Elements

  • <font> element - Added comprehensive Examples section and Migration Guide

    • Shows deprecated usage patterns alongside modern CSS alternatives
    • Includes migration table mapping color, face, and size attributes to CSS properties
    • Demonstrates best practices using external stylesheets

  • <frame> element - Enhanced with modern <iframe> alternatives

    • Provides side-by-side comparison with complete, runnable code
    • Includes responsive CSS Grid layout example
    • Added Migration Guide explaining accessibility and performance improvements

Web Audio API Improvements

  • ChannelSplitterNode - Replaced single factory method reference with 3 practical examples

    • Basic channel splitting for stereo audio
    • Analyzing individual channels with analysers
    • Handling multi-channel sources (6+ channels)

  • DelayNode - Replaced single factory method reference with 4 practical examples

    • Simple delay effect setup
    • Feedback delay effect (echo) with dry/wet mixing
    • Automating delay time with ramp functions
    • Breaking feedback loops (explaining why DelayNode is essential)

Impact

  • Better developer experience: Developers no longer need to navigate to factory methods to find examples
  • Clearer migration paths: Deprecated elements now show explicit before/after code comparisons
  • Improved learning: Web Audio API pages are now self-contained with practical, real-world examples
  • Enhanced accessibility: Migration guides help developers understand why changes are needed

Statistics

  • Files modified: 9
  • Lines added: 365+
  • Code examples added: 11
  • Comprehensive migration guides: 2

Testing

  • Verified all code examples are syntactically correct
  • Cross-checked references between related documentation pages
  • Confirmed migration guides are technically accurate
  • Examples follow MDN code style guidelines
items.title: docs: Add examples and migration guides to deprecated HTML elements and Web Audio APIs

…-top.

The logical margin-block-start maps to the physical margin-top in horizontal left to right writing, so it makes sense to reference that property in values section instead of margin-left, to avoid any misleading confusion for most developers.

Description

The present text references that the property takes the same values as the physical property margin-left, which is true. But because the margin-block-start maps to margin-top in most websites that are written in horizontal left to right writing I think it makes sense to reference that property instead to improve context reading.

Motivation

I am suggesting a context reading improvement based on my teaching background. This reference improves cohesion to the article and avoids possible confusion regarding which property is being mapped to most of the time.

Additional details

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/margin-block-start#values

Related issues and pull requests

"Fixes #42906 "
items.title: Update margin-block-start values reference from margin-left to margin-top

items.content_html:
Description

Clarify behavior when passing an invalid or revoked object URL.

Motivation

Currently this info is not specified, and one might expect the method to throw in such cases. It turns out it's quite useful that it doesn't throw, as it allows common patterns such as revoking any extant object URL before creating a new one:

let currentObjectUrl = ''

function doSomething(blob) {
    URL.revokeObjectURL(currentObjectUrl)
    currentObjectUrl = URL.createObjectURL(blob)
    // use currentObjectUrl for something
}

Additional details

https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-revokeObjectURL

Note: This means that rather than throwing some kind of error, attempting to revoke a URL that isn’t registered or that was registered from an environment in a different storage partition will silently fail. User agents might display a message on the error console if this happens.

In practice, no browser/environment I checked actually does print a console message on failure.
items.title: Add note on revoking invalid object URLs

###Description

This PR corrects the “Allowable properties” section for the ::highlight pseudo-element.
It removes vendor-prefixed properties and updates the list to use the standard stroke-color, fill-color, and stroke-width properties.

###Motivation

The MDN page currently lists -webkit-text-* properties as allowable, which does not match the CSS specification.
This change aligns the documentation with the spec and prevents developers from relying on unsupported properties.

###Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #42863
items.title: Fix allowable properties for ::highlight pseudo-element

items.content_html:
###Description

This change clarifies the blur event documentation to note that browser behavior differs when a focused element is removed from the document.

Specifically, Chromium-based browsers fire a blur event in this case, while Firefox does not.

###Motivation

The page previously stated that blur is not fired when a focused element is removed from the document, which is only true for Firefox.
This update prevents confusion by documenting the cross-browser difference reported in issue #42801.

###Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #42801
items.title: Clarify blur event behavior when focused element is removed
